In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ubiquinol form of CoQ 10 is a potent activator of the PPARα and LXRs/RXRα signaling pathways in SAMP1 mouse liver, and that this leads to increased expression of genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis and metabolism.
ubiquinol supplementation in SAMP1 animals induces a PPAR‐mediated increase of cholesterol biosynthesis, whereas the oxidized form has no such effect.

ubiquinol‐induced changes in gene expression and metabolism in SAMP1 liver tissue are related to PPARα and LX/RXR signalling pathways, but not to the oxidative state of the tissue or to the oxidative status of the CoQ10 molecule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reduced form of coenzme Q10 (Coq10H2) has a positive influence on cholesterol metabolism.
ubiquinol (the active form of CoQ) can be used for the prevention of atherosclerosis.
the reduced form of coQ10 mediates effects on cholesterol metabolism, at the transcriptional (gene expression) level as well as at the metabolite (cholesterol) level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reduced form of Q10 (ubiquinols) is more effective than its oxidized form (ubiquinones).
the reduced form of Q10 has distinct effects on cholesterol homeostasis in mice and that these effects are not apparent for the corresponding oxidized form of Q10.
the reduced form of coenzymes Q10 mediates effects on cholesterol metabolism in SAMP1 (senescent accelerated mouse prone 1) mice.
